notes: POWO and Flora of North America recognize Euphorbia cyathophora as accepted.
Older literature may place it under Poinsettia cyathophora or as a form/variety of Euphorbia heterophylla.

target_zone_range_leads.guardrail: Deep Review must verify exact target-zone counties.
leads: Master Plant Pool has 6 personal wild observations and marks Hays Local.
POWO lists Texas in the native range.
FNA includes Texas and describes the species as native to the midwestern/southeastern United States southward.
BONAP Euphorbia county maps should be used to document exact project counties.

morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Look at the floral bracts and the cyathial gland. E. cyathophora usually has sharply colored red/pink/orange or white bases on the upper bracts and a sessile to substipitate gland with an oblong opening and no annular rim.
diagnostic_traits: leaves may be linear, lanceolate, elliptic, or pandurate/lobed
upper floral bracts typically show strongly demarcated red, pink, orange, or white coloration at the base
cyathial gland opening oblong/flattened, without annular rim

confusers.separator: E. heterophylla usually has green or merely pale-based bracts and a stipitate gland with a circular opening and annular rim; E. cyathophora typically has sharply colored bract bases and an oblong gland opening.
